Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Inc. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing CloudForge Inc.'s results for the third quarter. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Mia Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Product Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Marketing Officer; David Kim, Chief Sales Officer; and Lisa Grant, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. CloudForge continued its strong growth trajectory in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included expanding our presence in emerging markets, accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform, enhancing our developer ecosystem, strengthening our commitment to sustainability, investing in employee training and development, improving cross-functional collaboration, and ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

Enterprise remains our highest-growth segment, now representing 62% of total revenue, up from 55% a year ago. We closed the quarter with $2.8 billion in new and expansion annual contract value—or ACV—across enterprise deals, a 28% year-over-year increase and well ahead of our internal guide of 20-25%. This momentum is fueled by net new logos, significant expansions with our top 100 customers, and competitive displacements where enterprises are consolidating on our hyperscale platform for AI, hybrid cloud, and mission-critical workloads.

Let me highlight a few marquee wins. First, we landed a landmark $450 million total contract value—or TCV—multi-year agreement with GlobalFin Trust, a top-10 global banking institution. This deal includes a full migration of their core trading and risk management platforms to our CloudForge Kubernetes-orchestrated environment, powered by our latest GenAI-optimized instances with integrated NVIDIA H100 GPUs. We're deploying over 50 petabytes of sovereign cloud storage compliant with both U.S. CISA guidelines and EU DORA regulations, enabling real-time fraud detection models that reduce latency by 40% compared to their legacy on-premises VMware setup. This marks our largest financial services win to date and expands our relationship with GlobalFin from $15 million ACV last year to over $120 million annualized.

In healthcare, we secured a $280 million TCV expansion with MediCore Health Systems, the leading U.S. provider network serving 80 million lives. Building on their initial 2022 migration, this accelerates their adoption of our serverless compute for HIPAA-compliant patient genomics workloads, leveraging our QuantumEdge network for sub-millisecond inference on foundation models fine-tuned with their proprietary datasets. Consumption has ramped 3x quarter-over-quarter, driven by our pay-as-you-go pricing, helping MediCore optimize costs amid budget scrutiny—echoing industry trends where 68% of healthcare CIOs cite TCO as their top cloud priority, per our CloudForge Enterprise Pulse survey.

On manufacturing, we displaced a major competitor with a $210 million TCV deal for AutoForge Industries, a Tier-1 EV supplier partnering with Tesla and Ford. This involves our Industrial IoT platform integrated with hybrid edge-to-cloud orchestration, handling 10 million sensors across global factories. Key was our Digital Twin Accelerator, cutting simulation times from days to hours using GPU-accelerated ray-tracing services, supporting their Industry 5.0 push.

Beyond headlines, we signed 17 deals over $10 million ACV, including eight net new logos—our strongest expansions since Q4 2022. 45% were competitive wins from Azure and Google Cloud, with customers citing 25% better price-performance on ML training and native open-source support like Ray and Kubeflow. Expansions drove 55% of ACV, top 20 clients up 42% YoY from AI ramp. Remaining performance obligations—or RPO—hit $18.2 billion, up 35% YoY, current RPO up 22%.

Regionally, Americas 68% of ACV, EMEA 40% YoY to 22% with a €150 million sovereign cloud from a German OEM via Frankfurt/Paris FedRAMP equivalence, APAC 52% YoY at 10% share with GPU clusters for telcos like NTT Docomo, offsetting China.

These wins validate our AI Everywhere thesis: 65% included CloudForge AI Suite, inference spend up 150% YoY, deals averaging 4.5 years. Cost optimization and multi-cloud via CloudBridge won hybrids. We expect $3.2 billion ACV in Q4, backed by $5 billion capacity expansion with 20 exaFLOPS AI compute, capturing IDC's $1.2 trillion market.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 24% year-over-year to $29.2 billion, exceeding our guidance. Our gross margin was 71%, reflecting our efficient cost structure. Our operating margin was 38%.

Good afternoon, everyone. Diving into top-line results, for the quarter ended September 30, 2024, total revenue was $29.2 billion, up 24% year-over-year from $23.6 billion, our 12th straight quarter of 20%+ growth amid AI and hybrid multi-cloud adoption.

We beat guidance of $28.0-$28.5 billion midpoint by 3.4%, or $970 million, from AI/ML ramp and enterprise pull-forward.

By segment: IaaS grew 28% to $17.8 billion (61%), with Graviton4 instances up 35%, 30-40% savings via spot/Savings Plans. PaaS/AI/ML surged 45% to $8.1 billion (28%), Bedrock AI up 60% QoQ inference, SageMaker UltraCluster traction. SaaS/other up 15% to $3.3 billion.

Regions: Americas $16.1 billion (55%, +25%) with DoD $2B sovereign; EMEA $6.4 billion (22%, +30%) GDPR zones, $500M sovereign; APAC $6.7 billion (23%, +18%) India/SE Asia, Mumbai H100.

Validating AI Everywhere, $10B YTD capacity incl. 2M Graviton4, 500K Trainium2. RPO $150 billion +42% YoY, 65% 12-month convert, NRR 128%. Gaining 200bps share to 32%, zero-ETL lakehouse, net-zero 2030.

This beat reflects execution, raising FY outlook.

Next, I'd like to introduce Mia Chen, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Mia Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in AI and machine learning services.

Good afternoon. Our technology advancements delivered record results, exceeding guidance across metrics amid AI workloads, hybrid architectures, infrastructure demand. Total revenue $29.2 billion, up 24% YoY and 5% QoQ, beating midpoint $850 million. 15th double-digit quarter, RPO +22% to $165 billion from bank migrations, auto AI.

Segments: IaaS $17.8 billion +28% (Graviton4, Nitro confidential, GPU +45% pharma drug discovery); PaaS $8.1 billion +17% (Kubernetes, LambdaForge Kafka +30% IoT); Data/AI $5.4 billion +28% (Bedrock/SageMaker 60%, Anthropic integrations, $1.2B ACV LLMs).

Profitability: GAAP gross 71%, non-GAAP 71.2% highest in 5Q via 15% power cut liquid cooling/renewables, net-zero 2035. Op income $10.8B +22%, non-GAAP op margin 38.1%, net $8.2B $1.72 EPS +12%, FCF $12.4B 43% revenue, cash $85B.

Customers: 1,200 net enterprise adds, 45 Fortune 100, dollar net expansion 128%, large (>1M) 62% revenue +14% ACV $4.5M.

Regions: Americas $16.1B 55% +24%, tech/finance; EMEA $6.4B 22% +21% sovereign Germany/France SAP; APAC $6.7B 23% +25% NTT/TSMC.

Capex $14.5B, 45 AZs Jakarta/Santiago, $2B quantum-safe, Fabric 85% Kubernetes, $500B hybrid market.

Q4 guide: $29.5-30.1B 17-19%, op income $11-11.4B, EPS $1.78-1.84. Positioned for macro, 95%+ SLAs.

Now, I'll pass it to Raj Patel for a product update.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Mia. We recently launched CloudForge Bedrock AI platform, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

Good afternoon. Before guidance, key metric: churn/retention via NDR, gross retention, logo churn—stickiness from AI/data/mission-critical.

Q3 NDR 118% +200bps YoY/flat QoQ, 11th >115% quarter vs industry 110%. Gross dollar retention 92% (contraction 8%), logo churn 4.2% overall/2.1% >$1M ARR.

Cohorts: 2022 122%, 2024 125% from Nimbus-like bundling.

Enterprise ($5M+ ARR 65%) NDR 125% +YoY, 70% 3-5yr contracts Hybrid Fabric, contraction 3%. SMB (20% ARR) 108% steady, churn 7.5% countered Pay-As-You-Go Plus +15% expansion ML Capacity Optimizer.

Regions: NA 120% 55% ARR GenAI +30%; EMEA 115% sovereignty SAP RISE; APAC 112% +YoY Japan/India 96% retention; LatAm/emerging 105%.

Drivers: Nimbus AI Suite vector DBs 40% TCO lower, Zero Trust VPCs; churn prediction retained 85% $45M ARR; TAM OKRs.

Pricing/packaging: 85% NDR from expansion, outcome SLAs. Gartner 85% multi-cloud, 60% wallet via Fabric, migration costs lock-in.

Q4 NDR 119-121%, FY 118-120%, 95% gross FY25.

I'll now hand it over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our marketing strategy.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Raj. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

Thank you. Before questions, energy efficiency/sustainability—core to profitability/leadership as #2 hyperscaler gaining on AWS 28% growth. Customers demand metrics, we deliver.

FY2023 PUE 1.18 vs 1.25/1.5 industry, 2.1M MWh saved +35% workloads AI 22% less energy.

Renewables 85% 25 PPAs 12GW, 100% 2025, 4.2GW new incl 1.5GW North Sea. Scope1/2 -28% 1.2M tCO2e +40% capacity, Scope3 supplier 50% renewables 2026.

Tech: Liquid cooling 60% US/EU -40%/rack AI 700W, 80% Q4'25; AetherOptix RL VM right-size -32% idle, 25% AI inference less vs Azure; heat reuse 150GWh VA, WUE 0.12 vs AWS 0.25.

Regions: EU 100% hourly Frankfurt/Paris VW Scope3; APAC solar-storage 70% 2026 Tokyo/Sydney; US IRA $800M Ohio/TX geothermal sub-1.1 PUE.

Tailwinds: 8% opex shave EBITDA 42%, 72% top100 RFP green Gartner 65% CIOs, Green Reservations +150% 10-15% premium. $5B 3yr quantum-dot/edge 1.05 PUE vs IEA 10% global power 2027.

Embedded flywheel: efficiency costs down, premiums up, moat.

Next, I'd like to introduce David Kim, who will provide an update on our sales performance.

David Kim:
Thank you, Elena. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

Good afternoon. Pricing strategies/discounting critical lever in competitive landscape.

Q3 revenue +28% $29.2B, consumption +32% $17.8B, effective pricing -4.2% YoY 3rd quarter compression, Gartner 3-5% erosion. NRR 118% +YoY fuels expansion.

Savings Plans/RIs $12.4B ARR equiv +42%, PAYG 38%, margins +210bps 72.8%, util 85% Graviton 40% perf.

Spot $890M 15% compute 65% disc, 92% util Auto-Scaling Pools +$250M AI training.

ASP compute $0.043/hr - , storage $0.022/GB, $180M headwind offset 15% volume, match AWS cuts promos.

Regions: NA 52% $16.1B +31% 22% disc premium AI $1.2M ARPU; EMEA 22% +25% 31% CUDs €500M EuroBank 70% margins; APAC 23% +42% 35% Flex-Pricing +18% share India zero-egress.

Value pricing: Sustainability 5-10% rebates Graviton ESG, ML engines +28% commitments RPO $45.2B +35% current.

FY25 2-3% erosion, Elite 65% GenAI $2B ARR. Discipline 8% promo cap margins 32%.

60% net ACV from discounting.

Finally, I'll pass it to Lisa Grant to discuss our security initiatives.

Lisa Grant:
Thank you, David. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Thank you. Data center expansion/capex cornerstone for hyperscale amid AI/edge/hybrid, Synergy $85B Q3 +25% AI 30%.

Q3 capex $2.8B 28% $10.1B rev +15% QoQ Nvidia H100/Blackwell PP&E 55% $1.54B servers 30% $840M.

FY24 guide $12.5-13.5B prior $11.5-12.5 20-25% up, 22-24% rev; 2025 $14-16B flat-up15%.

Capacity 48 zones 22 regions 1.2M racks +18% YoY 150MW Q, util 82%/90% ForgeOptix vs AWS 85% Azure 88%.

NA 55%: Ashburn-7/8 200MW renewable ForgeRack 1.2 PUE liquid GPU 10k H100s, Phoenix Edge 50MW Waymo; $1.6B Q capex $4B H2.

EMEA: Frankfurt-4 80MW EUCS ForgeSovereign, Paris-2 60MW Graviton25% TCO, Warsaw 200MW 95% renewable; $700M Q $2.5B ann.

APAC 25% growth: Singapore-3 120MW Jakarta subsea, Mumbai-2 90MW Jio ForgeBurst, HK-4 Tencent, Tokyo-3 quantum SBI; $500M Q $3B FY 28% IDC.

Emerging: Sao Paulo-2 70MW Sydney 150MW telco.

$500M Custom ForgeCore TPU 2x 40% power, 800Gbps NVMe-oF 99.9999%.

Efficiency capex/MW $8.5M -12% prefab 1.15 PUE, EBITDA 55% 2025 88% util.

Power 5GW PPA NuScale SMR, GPU stabilize.

22% share >Azure/Google, AI backbone.

Back to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks for taking my question. Can you provide more color on the outlook for Q4 revenue growth and any changes to full-year guidance given the strong enterprise momentum?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. We're raising our full-year revenue guidance to reflect the sustained AI demand and enterprise wins we highlighted. For Q4, we expect continued acceleration, targeting 25-27% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, building on the flywheel of expansions and AI inference scaling. Our capacity investments position us well to meet this without supply constraints, and RPO visibility supports multi-quarter strength. Happy to follow up offline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great, thank you. On the margin front, with pricing pressures and capex ramp, how should we think about gross and operating margins heading into FY25?

Jordan Lee:
Hi Emily, solid question. Our gross margins benefited from efficiency gains and commitment mix shifts this quarter, and we expect continued expansion to 71.5-72% in Q4 as utilization rises. Operating margins should hold in the high 37-39% range near-term, with opex discipline offsetting some capex. Into FY25, as capex moderates to 22% of revenue and renewables scale, we see room for 100bps+ expansion. Pricing discipline and AI premium services will be key tailwinds.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Thanks. Mia, curious about the AI roadmap—any updates on custom silicon or partnerships that could accelerate adoption?

Mia Chen:
Thanks, Mike. Yes, our ForgeCore custom silicon is on track for Q4 launch, delivering 2x inference throughput at lower power, complementing NVIDIA partnerships. We're deepening integrations with Anthropic and expanding UltraCluster for trillion-param models. Expect more announcements on ecosystem plays to drive PaaS growth beyond 45% in key markets.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
